outcome: Security posture across every cloud account is expressed on one severity scale that a small team can actually act on.
overview: A software company running in more than one cloud discovers that each provider’s own security tooling answers a different question in a different vocabulary, and nobody can state the company’s posture as a single fact. Prisma Cloud assesses configuration, workload and entitlement risk across the clouds in scope and expresses them on one severity scale. The thing that determines whether it works is unglamorous: findings only get fixed when each account has an owner, and the first honest deliverable is usually an account inventory nobody had.

benefits.text: Posture across several clouds is expressed on one severity scale rather than three vocabularies
benefits.limits: Coverage depth differs per provider and per service; a single scale can hide that unless the coverage matrix is published alongside it

benefits.text: Identity and entitlement sprawl becomes visible, which configuration scanning alone does not show
benefits.limits: Effective permission analysis is complex and its findings need engineering judgement; treating them as a work queue without triage generates noise

benefits.text: Checks can run in the pipeline, so a misconfiguration is caught before it is deployed
benefits.limits: The control plane is vendor-operated, so tenant region and log residency are design decisions to be made and recorded explicitly rather than properties of the product

residency: The control plane is vendor-operated; configuration metadata and findings leave the customer tenancy, and the tenant region is chosen and recorded at design

notFor.situation: A single-cloud estate well served by that provider’s native security services
notFor.why: The value here is a common view across providers; with one provider the native tooling is cheaper and closer

notFor.situation: An organisation already running another cloud-native application protection platform
notFor.why: Two posture platforms produce two finding sets, and reconciling them costs more than either resolves

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to onboarded accounts with findings routing to named owners
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed triage against an agreed severity policy.
1) Assessment — account inventory with owners, workload counts, existing findings and residency position
2) Design — severity policy, routing model, pipeline integration plan and the coverage matrix
3) Onboard — read-only connections, workload defenders, first severity tranche live
4) Enforce and hand over — pipeline checks moved from warn to block, operations handed over
deliverables: Every account in the inventory is connected, or is listed as an explicit exclusion
A finding of the highest severity reaches its account owner with a date attached
The published coverage matrix states, per provider and service, what is assessed and what is not
effort: 8–12 weeks to onboarded accounts with findings routing to named owners
